scope: Theorem 11.19 (Finite acyclic contour sewing) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 144. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let L, R : [0, T] → [0, ∞) be continuous, zero at the endpoints and strictly positive in between. On the circle C = [0, T]/(0 = T), let ∼c be the scalar contour relation s ∼c t ⇐⇒ c(s) = c(t) = min u∈[s,t] c(u), c ∈ {L, R}, with ordered representatives and the endpoint convention. Let ∼ be the relation generated by the two scalar relations. Suppose: (i) a finite constant M bounds the cardinality of every ∼-class; (ii) for every ∼-class E, the bipartite multigraph with vertices the L-classes and the R-classes in E, and one edge for each t ∈ E joining its two scalar classes, is a tree. Then C/ ∼ is homeomorphic to the sphere. The quotient map is continuous and its fibers are exactly the ∼-classes.
